newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures bounce to moderate gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures bounce to moderate gains.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures bounced up to moderate gains in early pit trading in a burst of good two-way activity.
Strength in U.S. Treasury bond futures, which slowly expanded gains, found added support from the dollar's rally.
The dollar hurdled technical levels as yawning interest rate differentials drew dollar-buyers and on sentiment that the dollar's intraday rise might not provoke central banks.
Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said Monday that G-10 countries see no reason for strong concern over recent developments in foreign exchange rates.

Although stock index futures prices climbed, traders said one primary dealer was a featured seller of some 500 June Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures near the outset. At the same time, it was seen as a buyer in Treasury bond futures.
They automatically labeled the firm's activity.
"Asset allocation," said one S&P 500 floor broker.

But they also said the rise in T-bond futures, which some said appeared guided by shortcovering after the recent decline tailed off, buoyed sentiment for some stock buyers who already were looking for a technical rise to correct recent hefty losses.
They noted that rising open interest in S&P 500 futures during Friday's turnaround to the upside suggested to some players that buyers were stepping in to snap up bargains.
Open interest in S&P 500 futures rose 3,887 contracts overall on Friday.
"So it means a lot of longs are piling in here," the floor broker said. "I would expect to see for the early part of this week people trying to square shorts from last week."
Technically, nearby S&P 500s managed to hurdle several resistance areas and probed above key resistance at 768.50, the low from March 27 when prices skidded to huge losses.
Fair value Monday stood at about 5.90 points over cash. Arbitrage buy programs would need roughly 6.70 points premium and sell programs would require about 5.20 points premium.

But index arbitrage was not a large factor after the opening bell, as the Dow Industrial Average jumped 50 points and triggered the New York Stock Exchange's curb in computer-assisted arbitrage programs.

At 1001 CDT/1501 GMT, June S&P 500s rose 6.20 to 768.80, Midcap rose 2.15 to 256.50, Russell rose 3.60 to 346.50, Value Line rose 5.95 to 693.70, NYSE Composite up 2.95 at 403.60, Nikkei fell 200.0 to 17,775.0, NASDAQ up 16.50 to 845.00.
